newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Wendy's earnings jump amid merger-related charge.
newsitem.headline: Wendy's earnings jump amid merger-related charge.

text.p: Wendy's International Inc., the fast-food restaurant chain, Wednesday reported higher fourth-quarter and full-year results.

Fourth-quarter profits jumped to $40.2 million, or 30 cents a share, compared with $18.2 million, or 15 cents a share, a year ago. Revenues for company-run stores, royalties and investment income rose to $488.8 million from $459.4 million.
Systemwide sales, including both company-run and franchised stores, rose 10 percent to $1.39 billion.
Chief Executive Gordon Teter said average sales per restaurant grew nearly 7 percent in U.S. stores during the quarter, including 10 percent in the month of December.

Teter said higher food costs and start-up costs for training and introduction of fresh stuffed pitas affected company margins. As a result, domestic operating margins decreased one-half point from a year ago, to 13.1 percent.
Earnings for the full year rose to $155.9 million, or $1.19 a share, compared with $110.1 million, or 88 cents a share, posted a year earlier.
Revenues were $1.90 billion vs. $1.75 billion, and systemwide sales rose 8 percent to $5.43 billion.

The company said Wendy's opened 343 restaurants, finishing the year with 4,933 restaurants open and 120 under construction. Tim Hortons, Canada's largest national chain of coffee and fresh baked goods, opened 200 stores and ended the year with 1,384 open and 64 under construction.
The Wendy's system totalled 6,317 restaurants worldwide.

Teter said the company's "aggressive but responsible growth strategy" will accelerate in 1997. "We plan to open or begin construction on 750 to 800 new Wendy's and Tim Hortons worldwide, including about 350 Wendy's in the U.S., 170 in international markets and 270 Tim Hortons."

Separately, Wendy's said the board of directors named Gordon Teter to the additional position of chairman, succeeding former Chairman Jim Near, who died last July. Teter, 53, retains the titles of chief executive officer and president, positions held since 1995 and 1991, respectively.
Wendy's stock fell 25 cents to $22.125 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
